statute_title: National Social Investment Programme Agency Act, 2023

sections.title: Objective
sections.content: 1.  The objective of this Act is to provide a legal and institutional framework for the establishment and management of the National Social Investment Programme in Nigeria.

sections.title: Application
sections.content: 2. This Act shall apply throughout the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

sections.title: Establishment of National Social Investment Programme
sections.content: 3.—(1) There is established the National Social Investment Programme (“in this Act referred to as “the Programme”) which shall consist of the following — (a)  N-Power Programme ; (b)  National Cash Transfer Programme ; (c)  National Home-Grown School Feeding Programme ; (d)  Government Enterprise and Empowerment Programme ; and (e)  such other Programme as may be approved by the President. (2) Each Programme shall have a National Programme Manager.
sections.part: Part II — National Social Investment Programme

sections.title: Beneficiaries of the Programme
sections.content: 4.—(1) The beneficiaries of the Programme under this Act shall be the poor and vulnerable which include — (a)  unemployed persons including unskilled persons ; (b)  vulnerable widows, orphans and children ; (c) persons with disabilities ; (d) vulnerable senior citizens ; and (e) such other category of persons as the National Social Investment Board may, with the approval of the President, determine by an order published in the Federal Government Gazette. (2)  The target beneficiaries of the Programme shall be as set out under the First Schedule to this Act.
sections.part: Part II — National Social Investment Programme

sections.title: Registration enrolment of beneficiaries of the Programme
sections.content: 5.—(1) The registration of beneficiaries of the Programme shall be open to all poor and vulnerable Nigerians. (2)  The selection and enrolment process shall be fair and reflect national spread. (3)  Where in the opinion of the Agency, an applicant is not qualified to benefit from the Programme, the Agency shall inform the applicant accordingly and provide the reasons.
sections.part: Part II — National Social Investment Programme

sections.title: National social register
sections.content: 6.—(1) There is established a National Social Register (in this Act referred to as “the Register”) which shall be deployed for implementing the Programme and any other related matter. (2)  The National Social Register shall contain the electronic information and data of poor and vulnerable persons and households from the 36 States and the Federal Capital Territory.
sections.part: Part II — National Social Investment Programme

sections.title: Termination of benefits
sections.content: 7.—(1) The Agency may cancel a beneficiary’s social investment benefits where such benefit has been obtained through misrepresentation, deceit, fraud or failure to disclose any material information. (2)  Any social investment benefits obtained through misrepresentation, deceit, fraud or failure to disclose any material information shall be refunded to the Government by the person or from his estate if he is deceased. (3)  The Agency may terminate the payment of social investment benefits to a beneficiary who is absent from Nigeria for a continuous period of six months. (4) The provision or payment of any social investment benefits to a beneficiary shall lapse when the — (a) person dies ; or (b) conditions upon which the person was considered a beneficiary no longer exist.
sections.part: Part II — National Social Investment Programme

sections.title: Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Agency
sections.content: 8.—(1) There is established the National Social Investment Programme Agency (“in this Act referred to as “the Agency”) for the proper execution and management of the Programme. (2)  The Agency shall — (a) be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal ; (b) may sue or be sued in its corporate name ; and (c) may acquire, mortgage and own movable or immovable property.
sections.part: Part III — Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Agency and its Governing Board

sections.title: Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Governing Board and Technical working Group
sections.content: 9.—(1) There is established for the Agency, the National Social Investment Programme Agency Board (in this Act referred to as “the Board”). (2) The Board shall consist of — (a) a Chairman who shall be a person of proven integrity with cognate experience in social investments ; (b) representatives of Federal Ministries responsible for the following, not below the rank of Director — (i)  humanitarian affairs, (ii) finance, (iii) education, (iv) health, (v) justice, (vi) women affairs, and (vii) agriculture ; (c) one representation each from the six geo-political zones ; and (d) the National Coordinator who shall also be the Secretary to the Board. (3)  Members of the Board other than ex-officio members shall be appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Minister. (4)  Members of the Board shall be paid such allowances as may be approved by the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission. (5)  The Chairman and members of the Board other than the National Coordinator shall hold office on part-time basis. (6)  The supplementary provisions set out under the Second Schedule to this Act shall apply to the proceedings of the Board. (7) The Board may for the purpose of exercising its powers under the Act, constitute a technical working group. (8)  The technical working group shall consist of the following — (a) The National Coordinator who shall be the Chairman ; (b) Chief Executives of the following agencies — (i) National Bureau of Statistics, (ii) Universal Basic Education Commission, (iii) National Primary Healthcare Development Agency, (iv) National Orientation Agency, (v) National Youth Service Corps, (vi) Central Bank of Nigeria, and (vii) such other agencies as the Board may determine ; (c) a representative each from the following bodies — (i)  Nigeria Governors Forum, (ii)  Civil Society Organisations, (iii) Organised Private Sector, (iv) International Development Partners, (v) International Non-Governmental Organisations, and (vi) Non-Governmental Organisations ; (d) Chairman of the State Coordinators Forum. (9) The technical working group shall perform the functions assigned to it by the Board.
sections.part: Part III — Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Agency and its Governing Board

sections.title: Tenure of office
sections.content: 10.—(1) Members of the Board other than ex-officio members shall hold office for a term of four years and may be reappointed for a further term of four years, and no more. (2) The appointment of members of the Board shall be on such terms and conditions as may be specified in their letters of appointment.
sections.part: Part III — Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Agency and its Governing Board

sections.title: Cessation of membership
sections.content: 11.—(1) The office of a member of the Board shall become vacant where — (a)  his term of office expires ; (b)  he resigns by notice in writing addressed to the Minister ; (c)  he dies ; (d)  he is declared bankrupt ; (e)  he is convicted of a felony or any offence involving dishonesty ; (f )  he is guilty of gross misconduct relating to his duties ; or (g)  in the case of an ex-officio member, he ceases to hold the office on the basis of which he is a member of the Board. (2)  Notwithstanding the provisions of section 10 of this Act and subsection (1), a member of the Board, may at any time be removed from office by the President for inability to discharge the duties of his office arising from infirmity of mind or body, misconduct or in the public interest. (3)  Where a vacancy occurs in the membership of the Board before the expiration of the term of office of a member, a fit and proper person shall be appointed for the remainder of the term to represent the same interest as the predecessor.
sections.part: Part III — Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Agency and its Governing Board

sections.title: Functions of the Agency
sections.content: 12.  The Agency shall — (a) oversee the implementation of policies, projects relating to the Programme ; (b) conduct overall monitoring, evaluation, impact assessment and review the implementation of the Programme ; (c) collaborate and interface with State Coordinators ; (d) maintain and facilitate the use of the National Social Register established under this Act ; (e) share national poverty maps to guide State Governments in the selection of the poorest Local Governments ; (f ) establish skill acquisition centres for the purpose of training of beneficiaries of the Programme and other persons ; (g) set periodic attainable targets for the implementation of the Programme ; (h)  develop regulations on accountability measures and mechanisms ; (i)  conduct overall monitoring, evaluation and review of the Programme ; (j)  prepare and submit annual reports on the implementation of the Programme to the Minister ; (k) designate inspectors or monitors, to such areas of Nigeria as it may determine, to inspect ongoing execution of the Programme by the Agency ; (l ) collaborate with the media on advocacy and mobilisation activities ; and (m) perform such other functions and exercise such powers as are incidental to the Programme.
sections.part: Part III — Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Agency and its Governing Board

sections.title: Powers of the Board
sections.content: 13.  The Board shall — (a) advise on the policy and strategic framework for the execution of the Programme for the implementation of the Agency ; (b) present timely annual reports to the President and the National Assembly, through the Minister, on the status of social investment programme and policy implementation in Nigeria ; (c) promote effective inter-governmental collaboration and co-operation in the Programme implementation ; (d) approve the appointments and conditions of service of staff of the Agency ; (e)  exercise disciplinary control over staff of the Agency ; and (f ) perform such other functions as may be necessary and expedient to achieve the objectives of this Act.
sections.part: Part III — Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Agency and its Governing Board

sections.title: Appointment of National Coordinator
sections.content: 14.—(1) There shall be for the Agency, a National Coordinator of Programme (“in this Act referred to as “the National Coordinator”) who shall be appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Minister and subject to confirmation by the Senate. (2) The National Coordinator shall — (a) be the Chief Executive and Accounting officer of the Agency ; (b) possess a university degree in the field of social sciences; agriculture, engineering, veterinary medicine or business administration ; (c) possess 10 years relevant managerial experience in the public or private sector five of which shall be on managerial level, in resource generation or poverty eradication systems ; (d) be advanced in computer literacy and data management ; (e) be a person of proven integrity and sound mental health ; and (f ) be accountable for the overall delivery of the execution of the Programme.
sections.part: Part IV — Staff of the Agency

sections.title: Tenure of office of the National Coordinator
sections.content: 15.—(1)  The National Coordinator shall hold office — (a)  for a term of four years and be eligible for reappointment for another term of four years and no more ; and (b)  on such terms and conditions as may be specified in his letter of appointment. (2) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1), the National Coordinator may be removed from office for inability to perform the functions of his office arising from infirmity of body or mind, for misconduct, or in the public interest.
sections.part: Part IV — Staff of the Agency

sections.title: Duties of the National Coordinator
sections.content: 16. The National Coordinator shall — (a) be responsible for the administration of the Agency ; (b) coordinate the implementation of all Programme with a view to achieving full integration, efficiency, effectiveness and impact ; (c) build sustainable partnerships with relevant stakeholders on the Programme ; (d) supervise all budgeting and procurement activities of the Programme ; (e) forge and ensure an effective monitoring and evaluation, and impact assessment on all activities of the Programme ; (f )  maintain all records and activities on the Programme and ensure the production of annual reports ; (g) take responsibility of assigning roles, supervision, training and assessment of all staff of the Programme ; (h) supervise the activities of all State Coordinators to ensure effectiveness, transparency, accountability and full coordination ; and (i)  carry out other assignments that are incidental to his office.
sections.part: Part IV — Staff of the Agency

sections.title: Other staff
sections.content: 17.—(1) The Agency may request for the deployment of such other staff from any Public Service of the Federation. (2)  Notwithstanding the provision of subsection (1), the Agency with the approval of the Board may employ directly such other staff as may be necessary. (3)  The Agency may where necessary, engage ad-hoc staff on contract to carry out projects and activities under the Programme. (4) Staff of the Agency shall, in respect of their service in the Agency, be entitled to pension and other retirement benefits prescribed in the Pension Reform Act.
sections.part: Part IV — Staff of the Agency

sections.title: Structure of the Agency
sections.content: 18.  For the effective performance of the functions of Agency, there shall be established for the Agency, the following Departments — (a) N-Power Programme Department ; (b) National Cash Transfer Programme Department ; (c) National Home-Grown School Feeding Programme Department ; (d) Government Enterprise and Empowerment Programme Department ; and (e) such other Departments and units as may be determined by the Agency.
sections.part: Part IV — Staff of the Agency

sections.title: Requirements for State Governments participation
sections.content: 19.—(1)  A State Government participating in the Programme under this Act shall — (a)  establish a State Social Investment Programme Agency ; (b) appoint a State Coordinator who shall — (i) possess 10 years relevant experience in the public or private sector five of which shall be on managerial level and not below the rank of a Director, (ii) be proficient in the use of computers for data collection, analysis and management, (iii) be a person of proven integrity and sound mental health, and (iv) be a State cabinet ranking appointee ; (c) provide office space, equipment and facilities for the administration of the Programme ; (d)  establish and manage the State Social Register ; (e) share State Social Register with the Agency ; and (f )  enter into a Programme Implementation Agreement with the Agency. (2) The State Coordinator shall — (a) be responsible for implementing the Programme in the State ; (b) act as a liaison between the State Government and the Agency ; and (c)  ensure full participation of the State Government in the implementation of the Programme.

sections.title: Establishment of the National Social Investment Programme Fund
sections.content: 20.—(1) There is established a fund for the Programme (“the Fund”) into which shall be credited — (a)  such sums as may be appropriated for the Programme by the National Assembly ; (b)  such sums as may be provided by the Federal Government to support the activities of the Agency or a particular Programme ; (c) sums accruing to the Agency by way of grants, gifts, donations, endowments and bequest made to the Agency for the purpose of the Programme ; (d)  money provided by individuals, companies, government institutions, bilateral or multilateral organisations and development partners and others for the purpose of the Programme ; (e) at least 5% of recovered repatriated funds ; and (f ) such other sums as may accrue to the Fund. (2) The Programme Fund shall be applied for the — (a) payment of benefits to beneficiaries of the Programme established under this Act ; (b) purpose of actualising the functions and powers of the Agency ; (c) payment of allowances and other benefits of members of the Board ; and (d)  such other purposes incidental to or connected with the attainment of the objectives of the Programme.

sections.title: Annual estimates and accounts
sections.content: 21.—(1) The Agency shall not later than 30 June in each financial year prepare and present to the Minister for approval, a statement of estimated income and expenditure of the Agency and the Programme for the following financial year. (2)  Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (1), the Agency may in any financial year, submit supplementary or adjusted statement of estimated income and expenditure of the Agency and the Programme to the National Assembly through the Minister. (3)  The Agency shall keep proper books of accounts, income, expenditure and surplus of the Fund in respect of each year and proper records in relation to those accounts and shall cause such accounts to be audited within six months after the end of each year by auditors appointed from the list supplied in accordance with the guidelines issued supplied by the Auditor-General for the Federation.

sections.title: Annual reports
sections.content: 22. The Agency with the approval of the Board shall prepare annual reports and accounts as at 31 March of each year and submit to the President, through the Minister not later than 30 June in each year a report on the activities of the Agency during the preceding year, and shall include in the report a copy of the audited accounts of the Fund of the Programme for that year and of the auditor’s report on it.

sections.title: Gifts to the office
sections.content: 23.  The Agency may accept gifts of movable or immovable properties from individuals or organisations in accordance with its mandate under this Act provided that the Agency shall not accept any gifts where the conditions of the offer are inconsistent with the functions and mandate of the Agency under this Act.

sections.title: Offences and penalties
sections.content: 24.  A person who knowingly — (a)  makes a false or misleading statement in any application under this Act, or (b) being gainfully employed, makes an application for enrolment in a Programme, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not more than N100,000, or imprisonment for a term of at least six months or both.

sections.title: Power of the President to give directives of general character to the Agency
sections.content: 25.  The Minister may give the Agency directives of a general or specific nature relating generally to the performance of its functions.

sections.title: Regulations and guidelines
sections.content: 26.—(1) The Board may, with the approval of the Minister, make regulations and issue guidelines generally for the purposes of giving effect to the provisions of this Act. (2) Notwithstanding the provision of subsection (1), regulations and guidelines made under this section may provide for — (a)  procedures to determine eligibility for social investment benefits under the Programme of the Agency ; (b)  implementation of the Programme by the Agency ; and (c) any other matter that may be considered expedient to actualise all or any of the Programmes established under this Act. (3)  The contravention of any regulations or guidelines issued under any of the provisions of this Act shall constitute an offence and shall be punishable as prescribed in the particular regulations or guidelines.

sections.title: Monitoring and evaluation
sections.content: 27. The Agency shall ensure the proper monitoring and evaluation of the executions and implementation of the Programme and shall — (a) issue guidelines to regulate standards ; and (b) enforce compliance with quality requirements.

sections.title: Premises
sections.content: 28.  For the purpose of providing office premises for the performance of the functions of the Agency, the Agency may subject to the Land Use Act — (a) purchase or take on lease, any land, building or property ; (b) build, equip and maintain offices and premises ; or (c) let, lease or sell out any offices or premises held by it which it no longer requires for the performance of its functions under this Act.

sections.title: Pre-action notice
sections.content: 29.—(1)  A civil action shall not be commenced against the Agency or its authorised officers before the expiration of a period of 30 days after written notice of intention to commence the suit shall have been served on the Agency by the intending plaintiff or his agent, and the notice shall clearly state the — (a) cause of action ; (b)  particulars of the claim ; (c)  name and place of abode of the intending plaintiff ; and (d) relief sought. (2)  A notice, summons or other document required or authorised to be served upon the Agency under the provisions of this Act or any other law may be served by delivering it to the Agency or the Minister.

sections.title: Restriction on execution against property of the Agency
sections.content: 30.  In any action or suit against the Agency, no execution shall be levied or attachment process issued against the Agency, unless at least three months’ notice of the intention to execute or attach has been given to the Agency.

sections.title: Limitation of suits against the Agency
sections.content: 31.—(1)  Subject to the provisions of this Act, the provisions of the Public Officers Protection Act shall apply in relation to any suit against any member of the Board, officer or staff of the Agency. (2)  Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, no suit shall lie against the Agency, any member of the Board, the National Coordinator or any other officer or staff of the Agency for anything done under this Act or any other law, or any alleged neglect or default in the execution of this Act or such law, duty or authority, unless — (a) it is commenced within three months after the act, neglect or default complained of ; or (b) in the case of a continuation of damage or injury, within six months next after the ceasing of such damage or injury.

sections.title: Savings and transitional provisions
sections.content: 32.—(1) The right, interest, obligation, proceedings, assets and liability of the National Social Investment Office existing before the commencement of this Act shall by virtue of this Act be deemed to be that of the Agency established under this Act, to the extent that they are consistent with any of the provisions of this Act. (2)  Any reference to the National Social Investment Office existing before the commencement of this Act or a document issued in the name of the National Social Investment Office existing before the commencement of this Act, shall be read, unless the context otherwise requires, as a reference to the Agency established under this Act.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.content: 33. In this Act — “Agency” means the National Social Investment Programme Agency ; “beneficiary” means a person who receives social investment benefits under any Programme established under this Act ; “lDPs” means Internally Displaced Persons ; “LGAs” means Local Government Areas which shall where appropriate, include Area Councils recognised by law ; “Minister” means the Minister responsible for matters relating to humanitarian affairs ; “Ministry” means the Ministry responsible for matters relating to humanitarian affairs ; “National Coordinator” means the coordinator of the Programme and administrative head of the Agency ; “NSIP” means National Social Investment Programme ; “Programme Manager” means head of each of the Programmes ; “President” means the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria; “Programme” means National Social Investment Programme established under this Act ; “State Coordinator” means administrative head of the Programme appointed by a State Government ; and “State Government” means the Government of a State of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

sections.title: Citation
sections.content: 34.  This Act may be cited as the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023.
